quote: splitting your code into multiple files. Especially react components can and should be separated into atomic components and custom hooks.
statement: In frontend/**, React components should be split into atomic components and custom hooks rather than kept in large files.

quote: extracting types and interfaces into `.d.ts` files.
statement: In frontend/**, types and interfaces should be extracted into separate .d.ts files to keep files short.

quote: We prefer lambda functions over the `function` keyword.
statement: In frontend/**, functions should be declared as arrow functions (const x = () => ...) rather than with the `function` keyword.

quote: Simple functions, that return a value can be shortened to one-liners.
statement: In frontend/**, simple value-returning arrow functions should use the concise expression body (one-liner) form.

quote: Names of functions should - be as short as possible while clearly communicating their purpose. - not include technical details, if not necessary. - avoid abbreviations.
statement: In frontend/**, function names should be short, purpose-describing, free of unnecessary technical details and must avoid abbreviations (e.g. not clcX, doStuffWithX).
In frontend/**, every function must have an ESDoc (/** ... */) comment.

quote: Please make sure that your documenation can be read in a standard text editor (hard line breaks at ~120 characters, etc.).
statement: In frontend/**, ESDoc comments should be hard-wrapped at about 120 characters.

quote: explain what the function does. If the explanation is longer than one line, then write a short introdoctory first line, followed by a break and then the longer explanation.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must explain what it does; multi-line explanations must start with a short introductory line followed by a break.

quote: contain every parameter with the `@param name explaination` annotation, that explains the purpose of the parameter.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain an `@param name explanation` annotation for every parameter.

quote: contain a `@return description` annotation if the return type isn't `void`, that explains the meaning of the value.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain an `@return description` annotation if the return type is not void.

quote: contain `@throws ErrorClass description` annotations if the function throws runtime errors or doesn't catch errors from other method calls.
statement: In frontend/**, a function's ESDoc must contain `@throws ErrorClass description` annotations if the function throws or does not catch errors from called methods.

quote: contain a blank line between the description and the annotation block.
statement: In frontend/**, ESDoc comments must have a blank line between the description and the annotation block.

quote: The described annotations must appear in this order: `@param`, `@return`, `@throws`
statement: In frontend/**, ESDoc annotations must appear in the order @param, @return, @throws.

quote: Every exported type and interface must have an [ESDoc](https://esdoc.org/). No special annotations are needed.
statement: In frontend/**, every exported type and interface must have an ESDoc comment.
In frontend/**, React components must be function components, not class components.

quote: must be functional. Use the `React.FC` type.
statement: In frontend/**, React components must be typed with `React.FC` (e.g. `const X: React.FC<XProps> = ...`).

quote: can omit the `@return` annotation in the ESDoc if it returns always the same React DOM.
statement: In frontend/**, React component ESDocs may omit the @return annotation when the component always returns the same React DOM.

quote: should use the [`useCallback`](https://reactjs.org/docs/hooks-reference.html#usecallback) hook where possible. Don't use inline functions.
statement: In frontend/**, React components should wrap handler functions in `useCallback` and must not pass inline functions (e.g. as JSX props).

quote: should use [custom hooks](https://reactjs.org/docs/hooks-custom.html) to extract long functions to reduce the number of lines in the component file.
statement: In frontend/**, React components should extract long functions into custom hooks.

quote: must be placed in files that have the same name as the component, but in [kebab-case](https://stackoverflow.com/a/17820138). This file can also contain the interface for the properties.
statement: In frontend/**, each React component must live in a file named after the component in kebab-case (e.g. IncrementNumberButton in increment-number-button.tsx); the props interface may live in the same file.
In frontend/**, React components should be named in PascalCase.

quote: Don't log directly to the console. Use our logging class `Logger` in "src/utils".
statement: In frontend/**, code must not log via `console.*`; it must use the `Logger` class from frontend/src/utils/logger.ts.

quote: Create one instance of `Logger` per file. Don't pass or share the instances.
statement: In frontend/**, each file must create its own single `Logger` instance and must not pass or share Logger instances across files.

quote: The first argument of the constructor is the scope. Use the name of the class or component whose behaviour you want to log or choose an explanatory name.
statement: In frontend/**, `new Logger(scope)` must be given a scope that is the name of the logging class or component (or an explanatory name).

quote: If you want to add a sub scope (because e.g. you have two components that are similar or are used together, like the sub-classes of the iframe communicator), separate the main and sub scope with " > ".
statement: In frontend/**, Logger scopes with a sub scope must separate main and sub scope with " > " (e.g. new Logger('Main > Sub')).

quote: Scopes should be upper camel case.
statement: In frontend/**, Logger scope strings should be UpperCamelCase.

quote: Log messages should never start with a lowercase letter.
statement: In frontend/**, log messages passed to Logger methods must not start with a lowercase letter.

quote: Log messages should never end with a colon or white space.
statement: In frontend/**, log messages passed to Logger methods must not end with a colon or whitespace.

quote: Because we need to have empty constructors in our entity classes for TypeORM to work, the actual constructor is a separate `create` method.
statement: In backend entity classes, constructors must be empty and instances must be built via a separate static `create` method.

quote: Only require the non-optional properties of the corresponding entity
statement: In backend entity classes, the `create` method should only take the entity's non-optional properties as parameters (exceptions must be documented in the method doc).
In backend entity classes, the `create` method should have no optional parameters (exceptions must be documented in the method doc).

quote: Have no lists which can be empty (so probably most of them)
statement: In backend entity classes, the `create` method should not take list parameters that can be empty.

quote: Should either return a complete and fully useable instance or return a Pick/Omit type.
statement: In backend entity classes, the `create` method should return either a complete entity instance or a Pick/Omit type of the entity.

quote: Each of those files (except `auth.config.ts` which is discussed later) consists of three parts: 1. An interface 2. A Joi schema 3. A default export
statement: In backend/src/config/*.config.ts, each config file must consist of a config interface, a validation schema and a default export that builds and validates the config.

quote: All enums that are used in here are put in their own files with the extension `.enum.ts`.
statement: In backend/src/config/**, enums used in config interfaces must be defined in their own files with the `.enum.ts` extension.

quote: The most important part here is that each value ends with `.label()`. This names the environment variable that corresponds to each config option.
statement: In backend/src/config/*.config.ts, each schema value must end with `.label()` naming the corresponding environment variable.

quote: The error messages are piped into the util method `replaceAuthErrorsWithEnvironmentVariables`.
statement: In backend/src/config/auth.config.ts, validation error messages must be passed through `replaceAuthErrorsWithEnvironmentVariables`.

quote: Some config files also have a `.mock.ts` file which defines the configuration for the e2e tests. Those files just contain the default export and return the mock config object.
statement: In backend/src/config/**, `.mock.ts` config files should contain only a default export returning the mock config object.

quote: The config for the `EventEmitterModule` is stored in `events.ts` and exported as `eventModuleConfig`. In the same file enums for the event keys are defined.
statement: In backend, the EventEmitterModule config must live in backend/src/events.ts exported as `eventModuleConfig`, and event-key enums must be defined in that same file.

quote: In the enum definition a comment should tell you what exactly this value should be.
statement: In backend/src/events.ts, each event-key enum member should have a comment describing the value sent with the event.

quote: Each storage backend needs to implement an interface with three methods: `saveFile(uuid, buffer, fileType)` ... `deleteFile(uuid, metadata)` ... `getFileUrl(uuid, metadata)`
statement: In backend media storage backends, each backend must implement the media backend interface with `saveFile(uuid, buffer, fileType)`, `deleteFile(uuid, metadata)` and `getFileUrl(uuid, metadata)`.

quote: Therefore, the migrations and database types use their own CommonJS package.
statement: In backend, Knex migrations and database types are kept in their own CommonJS package rather than importing from backend TypeScript or commons.

quote: "hedgedoc-local/correct-logger-context": "error" (backend/.oxlintrc.json:11) - 'Ensure logger context strings match the method name where they are called'
statement: In backend/**, calls of the form `this.<x>.logger.{error,log,warn,debug,verbose}(message, 'context')` with a string-literal second argument must pass the name of the enclosing class method as the context string.
scope: backend/** class methods calling the logger

statement: In backend/**, code should not have unused variables; unused arguments must be named with underscores only (^_+$).

In backend/**, code must not stringify values whose toString() is the default Object toString (e.g. objects in template literals or String()).
